reasons: F01, F02: material weakness in internal control tied to staffing/segregation of duties, a weak control environment typical of small reporters where errors and override are more likely
F04, F21: going-concern doubt plus a capital raise in the year or planned creates strong pressure to present favorable results to investors and lenders
F05, F15: auditor change within two years and an interim/acting CFO point to instability in the finance function and in audit oversight
F11: material related-party transactions are a common way to misstate results and are harder to verify in a small company with poor controls
F03: no auditor ICFR attestation (non-accelerated filer), so the control weakness was not independently tested
F24: the critical audit matter is revenue, which the auditor itself identified as a high-risk area
F06, F07, F16, F17, F18: no disagreements with the accountants, no prior-period corrections and no investigations or class actions, which limits evidence of actual misstatement
R01-R19: all ratios are n/a, so the quantitative screens (Beneish M, Dechow F, accruals) cannot confirm or offset the qualitative red flags
